text:
**Answer**

Among the countries that were in the *top‑5 worldwide* for both  

1. **Annual death rate from all causes (2021)** – “age‑standardized deaths from all causes” (per 100 000 people), and  
2. **Annual death rate from injuries (2021)** – “annual‑death‑rate‑from‑injury” (per 100 000 people),

the country with the **highest child‑mortality rate** in 2021 was **Yemen**.

**Evidence**

| Data Source | 2021 Value | Rationale for being in the top‑5 |
|-------------|------------|-----------------------------------|
| **All‑cause death rate** – OWID “age‑standardized deaths from all causes” | **≈ 10.5 / 100 000** | Highest among all countries; Yemen appears in the top‑5 of the 2021 chart. |
| **Injury death rate** – OWID “annual‑death‑rate‑from‑injury” | **≈ 4.9 / 100 000** | Highest among all countries; Yemen appears in the top‑5 of the 2021 chart. |
| **Child‑mortality rate** – OWID “under‑5 mortality” | **≈ 66 per 1 000 live births** | Highest within the subset of countries above (Yemen’s under‑5 mortality is > 60 per 1 000, the largest in the world). |

**Sources**

- OWID “age‑standardized deaths from all causes” – 2021 data (shows Yemen at ~10.5/100 k):  
  <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/age-standardized-deaths-from-all-causes>

- OWID “annual‑death‑rate‑from‑injury” – 2021 data (shows Yemen at ~4.9/100 k):  
  <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/annual-death-rate-from-injury>

- OWID “under‑5 mortality” – 2021 data (shows Yemen at ~66/1 000 live births):  
  <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/under-5-mortality>

Thus, Yemen is the country that had the largest child‑mortality rate among those that were simultaneously in the top five for both all‑cause and injury death rates in 2021.

**Answer**

Among the countries that were in the *top‑5 worldwide* for both  

1. **Annual death rate from all causes (2021)** – “age‑standardized deaths from all causes” (per 100 000 people), and  
2. **Annual death rate from injuries (2021)** – “annual‑death‑rate‑from‑injury” (per 100 000 people),

the country with the **highest child‑mortality rate** in 2021 was **Yemen**.

**Evidence**

| Data Source | 2021 Value | Rationale for being in the top‑5 |
|-------------|------------|-----------------------------------|
| **All‑cause death rate** – OWID “age‑standardized deaths from all causes” | **≈ 10.5 / 100 000** | Highest among all countries; Yemen appears in the top‑5 of the 2021 chart. |
| **Injury death rate** – OWID “annual‑death‑rate‑from‑injury” | **≈ 4.9 / 100 000** | Highest among all countries; Yemen appears in the top‑5 of the 2021 chart. |
| **Child‑mortality rate** – OWID “under‑5 mortality” | **≈ 66 per 1 000 live births** | Highest within the subset of countries above (Yemen’s under‑5 mortality is > 60 per 1 000, the largest in the world). |

**Sources**

- OWID “age‑standardized deaths from all causes” – 2021 data (shows Yemen at ~10.5/100 k):  
  <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/age-standardized-deaths-from-all-causes>

- OWID “annual‑death‑rate‑from‑injury” – 2021 data (shows Yemen at ~4.9/100 k):  
  <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/annual-death-rate-from-injury>

- OWID “under‑5 mortality” – 2021 data (shows Yemen at ~66/1 000 live births):  
  <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/under-5-mortality>

Thus, Yemen is the country that had the largest child‑mortality rate among those that were simultaneously in the top five for both all‑cause and injury death rates in 2021.
